problems.title: Move a signed factor inside a square root
problems.question: Write $-ab^3\sqrt{-a^3/b^5}$ with the outside factor under the square-root sign, using real square roots.
problems.idea: Check the sign of the outside factor before moving its square inside.
formulas: A real square root requires a nonnegative radicand.
steps: The original expression requires $b\ne0$ and $-a^3/b^5\ge0$. Since these powers are odd, this means $a/b\le0$, equivalently $ab\le0$.
Thus $ab^3=(ab)b^2\le0$, so the outside factor $-ab^3$ is nonnegative.
It may therefore be moved inside as its square: $\sqrt{(-ab^3)^2(-a^3/b^5)}$.
Multiply powers: $a^2b^6(-a^3/b^5)=-a^5b$.
problems.answer: $\sqrt{-a^5b}$ (option დ), on the original real domain $b\ne0$, $ab\le0$.

problems.title: Clear fractions and retain excluded values
problems.question: Solve $\frac{x+3}{x}+4\frac{x}{x-2}=5$.
problems.idea:
The fractions require $x
e0,2$; multiply by $x(x-2)$ to obtain a linear equation after cancellation.
formulas: Multiplying an equation by a nonzero common denominator preserves its solutions on the original domain.
steps: The domain is $x\ne0,2$.
Multiply through: $(x+3)(x-2)+4x^2=5x(x-2)$.
This root is neither $0$ nor $2$, so it is valid.

problems.title: Intersect two inequality solution sets
problems.question: Solve the system $\frac25x-\frac13<\frac15x+\frac53$ and $\frac13(x-2)\ge\frac16(x-6)$.
problems.idea: Solve each inequality separately, then keep only numbers satisfying both.
formulas: A system of inequalities uses the intersection of their solution sets.
Multiplication by a positive denominator preserves the inequality direction.
steps: For the first inequality, subtract $x/5$ and add $1/3$: $x/5<2$, so $x<10$.
For the second, multiply by $6$: $2(x-2)\ge x-6$.
This becomes $2x-4\ge x-6$, hence $x\ge-2$.
Both conditions hold exactly when $-2\le x<10$.
problems.note: The second inequality is missing from the converted quiz PDF. It was recovered from the original Word document’s embedded equation and is included in the question above.

problems.title: A difference of two conjugate squares
problems.question: Evaluate $\dfrac{(2+\sqrt3)^2-(2-\sqrt3)^2}{8\sqrt3}$.
problems.idea: The terms containing squares cancel; only the opposite cross terms remain.
steps: Use $u=2$ and $v=\sqrt3$: the numerator is $4\cdot2\sqrt3=8\sqrt3$.
The denominator is the same nonzero number, so the quotient is $1$.

problems.title: Recover trapezoid bases from its midline
problems.question: A diagonal divides the midline of an isosceles trapezoid into lengths $2$ cm and $5$ cm. A leg is $6$ cm. Find its angles.
problems.idea: The two midline pieces are half the two bases. The base difference supplies each leg’s horizontal projection.
formulas: A triangle midsegment is half its parallel side.
In an isosceles trapezoid, each leg’s horizontal projection is half the base difference.
A right-triangle leg equal to half the hypotenuse is opposite $30^\circ$.
steps: The diagonal cuts the midline into half-base lengths, so the bases are $4$ cm and $10$ cm.
Each leg projects horizontally by $(10-4)/2=3$ cm.
In the resulting right triangle, the hypotenuse is the $6$ cm leg and its horizontal leg is $3$ cm, half the hypotenuse.
The angle opposite that $3$ cm leg is $30^\circ$, so the acute angle with the base is $60^\circ$.
Angles along a leg are supplementary, so the obtuse angle is $120^\circ$.
problems.answer: Two $60^\circ$ angles and two $120^\circ$ angles (option დ).

problems.title: The sign of a radical coefficient
problems.question: Solve $(2\sqrt2-3)(1-3x)>0$.
problems.idea: Determine the sign of the fixed first factor before dividing.
formulas: For nonnegative numbers, squaring preserves order.
Dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses its direction.
steps: Compare $2\sqrt2$ and $3$ by squaring: $8<9$, so $2\sqrt2-3<0$.
A product with a negative first factor is positive only if the second factor is negative.
Thus $1-3x<0$, giving $x>1/3$.

problems.title: Join the midpoints of a quadrilateral
problems.question: A quadrilateral has diagonals of lengths $6$ and $8$. Join the midpoints of its consecutive sides. Find the new quadrilateral’s perimeter.
problems.idea: Each new side is a triangle midsegment parallel to one original diagonal.
formulas: A triangle midsegment has half the length of its parallel third side.
steps: Two opposite new sides are each half the $6$-unit diagonal, so each is $3$.
The other two are each half the $8$-unit diagonal, so each is $4$.
The perimeter is $3+4+3+4=14$.

problems.title: Square roots of squared opposites
problems.question: For which real $x$ does $\sqrt{x^2}=\sqrt{(-x)^2}$ hold?
problems.idea: Opposite numbers have the same square, and the principal square root returns their common absolute value.
steps: The two radicands are identical and nonnegative for every real input.
Both sides equal $|x|$, including when $x$ is negative or zero.

problems.title: An interval with a central gap
problems.question: Solve $|x|<5$ and $|x-2|\ge1$ simultaneously.
problems.idea: The first condition gives a bounded interval; the second removes points less than one unit from two.
formulas: $|x-c|\ge r$ means $x\le c-r$ or $x\ge c+r$ for $r>0$.
steps: The first solution set is $(-5,5)$.
The second is $x\le1$ or $x\ge3$.
Intersect these: $-5<x\le1$ or $3\le x<5$.
The endpoints $1,3$ are included because the second inequality is non-strict; $-5,5$ are excluded by the first.

problems.title: The fourth angle of a cyclic quadrilateral
problems.question: Three consecutive angles of a cyclic quadrilateral have ratio $1:3:5$. Find the fourth angle.
problems.idea: The first and third of three consecutive angles are opposite.
formulas: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180^\circ$.
steps: Write the given angles as $t,3t,5t$.
The first and third sum to $6t=180^\circ$, so $t=30^\circ$.
The second angle is $3t=90^\circ$. The fourth is opposite it, so it is $180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$.

problems.title: Circumradius of an isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base $12$ and altitude to the base $9$. Find its circumradius.
problems.idea: Find the equal sides and area first, then use the circumradius formula.
steps: The altitude bisects the base, so each half is $6$. The equal side satisfies $s^2=9^2+6^2=117$.
The area is $\Delta=12\cdot9/2=54$.
The product of the three sides is $12s^2=12\cdot117=1404$.

problems.title: A secant whose external part is half its total
problems.question: From the same external point, a tangent has length $4$. A secant’s nearer circle intersection is the midpoint of the entire secant segment. Find the full secant length.
problems.idea: Apply the tangent-secant power relation.
formulas: Tangent length squared $=(\text{external secant part})(\text{full secant length})$.
steps: Let the full secant length be $L>0$. Its external part is $L/2$.
The power relation gives $4^2=(L/2)L=L^2/2$.
Thus $L^2=32$ and $L=4\sqrt2$.

problems.title: Two similar trapezoids
problems.question: A line parallel to the bases divides a trapezoid into two similar trapezoids. The original bases are $1$ and $9$. Find the section length.
problems.idea: Corresponding base lengths of the two smaller trapezoids must have equal ratios.
formulas: If the section length is $s$, similarity gives $s/1=9/s$.
steps: The upper trapezoid has bases $1,s$; the lower has bases $s,9$.
Similarity gives $s^2=1\cdot9=9$.
Lengths are positive, so $s=3$.

problems.title: A rhombus with angle difference 120 degrees
problems.question: A rhombus has inradius $2$, and two of its angles differ by $120^\circ$. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Adjacent rhombus angles sum to 180 degrees. The incircle diameter equals the height.
formulas: A side opposite $30^\circ$ in a right triangle is half the hypotenuse.
steps: Let the smaller angle be $\theta$. The larger is $180^\circ-\theta$, so $180^\circ-2\theta=120^\circ$. Thus $\theta=30^\circ$.
The height is the incircle diameter $h=4$.
In the right triangle formed by a side and an altitude, this height is opposite $30^\circ$, so the side is $2h=8$.
The perimeter is $4\cdot8=32$.

problems.title: A square in a right triangle
problems.question: A square is inscribed in a right triangle with legs $6$ and $9$, sharing the triangle’s right-angle vertex and having its opposite corner on the hypotenuse. Find its side.
problems.idea: Use the intercept equation of the hypotenuse with the square’s opposite vertex $(s,s)$.
formulas: A line joining $(a,0)$ and $(0,b)$ has equation $x/a+y/b=1$.
steps: Place the two triangle legs on the coordinate axes. The hypotenuse is $x/6+y/9=1$.
The square’s opposite vertex $(s,s)$ lies there, so $s/6+s/9=1$.
The coefficient is $1/6+1/9=5/18$. Thus $5s/18=1$ and $s=18/5=3.6$.

problems.title: A right angle from two externally tangent circles
problems.question: Two circles touch externally at $A$. A common external tangent touches them at $B,C$. Find $\angle BAC$.
problems.idea: The tangent at $A$ meets the common tangent at a point equally distant from $A,B,C$.
formulas: Tangent segments from a common external point are equal.
An angle subtended by a diameter is $90^\circ$.
steps: Let $P$ be the intersection of the tangent at $A$ with line $BC$.
Tangency to the first circle gives $PA=PB$; tangency to the second gives $PA=PC$.
In the external-tangency configuration, $P$ lies between $B,C$, so it is the midpoint of $BC$.
Thus $A,B,C$ lie on a circle centred at $P$, with $BC$ as diameter. Therefore $\angle BAC=90^\circ$.

problems.title: Distance between two incircle contact points
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides $15$ and base $10$. Find the distance between the incircle’s contact points on the equal sides.
problems.idea: Equal tangent lengths locate the two contact points; their joining segment is parallel to the base.
formulas: Tangent segments from one vertex are equal.
In an isosceles triangle, equal fractional distances along its equal sides determine a segment parallel to the base.
Similar triangles have proportional corresponding sides.
steps: Let the apex be $B$ and base vertices $A,C$. The incircle touches the base at its midpoint, so each base tangent length is $5$.
Each equal side therefore has $5$ units from its base vertex to the contact point and $15-5=10$ units from $B$.
The two contacts are at fraction $10/15=2/3$ of the distance from $B$ along the equal sides.
The triangle they form with $B$ is similar to the full triangle, so their separation is $(2/3)\cdot10=20/3$.

problems.title: Area between a V-shaped graph and a horizontal line
problems.question: Find the area of the region satisfying $y\ge|x|$ and $y\le2$.
problems.idea: The boundaries form a triangle with its top edge on $y=2$.
steps: The triangle’s vertices are $(0,0),(-2,2),(2,2)$.
The horizontal base has length $2-(-2)=4$. Its perpendicular height from the origin is $2$.
The area is $4\cdot2/2=4$ square units.

problems.title: Collect constants and radical terms
problems.question: Evaluate $(5-\sqrt3)^2+(1+2\sqrt3)^2+(5-\sqrt3)(1+\sqrt3)$.
problems.idea: Expand each product and collect the ordinary and square-root terms separately.
steps: Add: the constants give $43$, and the radical coefficient is $-10+4+4=-2$.

problems.title: Reduce radicals to a common square root
problems.question: Evaluate $\dfrac{\frac13\sqrt{72}-\frac14\sqrt8+\frac1{10}\sqrt{50}}{2\sqrt2}$.
problems.idea: Extract perfect squares so every term in the numerator is a multiple of $\sqrt2$.
steps: $\sqrt{72}=6\sqrt2$, $\sqrt8=2\sqrt2$, and $\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2$.
The numerator is $2\sqrt2-\frac12\sqrt2+\frac12\sqrt2=2\sqrt2$.
Divide by $2\sqrt2$ to get $1$.

problems.title: Harvesting with more identical machines
problems.question: Five identical combine harvesters harvest $300$ hectares in one day. How many hectares can seven harvest in one day?
problems.idea: At the same working rate and time, output is proportional to the number of machines.
steps: One combine harvests $300/5=60$ hectares per day.
Seven harvest $7\cdot60=420$ hectares per day.

problems.title: Factor a difference of cubes containing a radical
problems.question: Simplify $\frac{\sqrt y}{27-y\sqrt y}\left(1+\frac3{\sqrt y}+\frac9y\right)$.
problems.idea: Set $t=\sqrt y$ to turn the expression into a rational function in $t$.
steps: The original domain is $y>0$, $y\ne9$: denominators require nonzero $\sqrt y,y$, and $27-y\sqrt y$.
The bracket becomes $(t^2+3t+9)/t^2$, while the first factor is $t/(27-t^3)$.
Factor the difference of cubes and cancel $t^2+3t+9$ to obtain $1/[t(3-t)]$.
Replace $t$ by $\sqrt y$: the result is $1/(3\sqrt y-y)$.

problems.title: A parameter giving a positive root
problems.question: For which real $t$ does $3(2-x)=4(t-2x)$ have a positive solution $x$?
problems.idea: Solve for $x$ in terms of the parameter, then require that expression to be positive.
steps: Expand: $6-3x=4t-8x$.
Add $8x-6$ to both sides: $5x=4t-6$, so $x=(4t-6)/5$.
Since $5>0$, this is positive exactly when $4t-6>0$.
Thus $t>3/2$.

problems.title: Extract a factor without losing its absolute value
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt{-a^6b^3/c^3}$ using real square roots.
problems.idea: A square root of a square gives an absolute value. Also keep track of the real domain, including the zero case.
steps: The original denominator requires $c\ne0$. If $a=0$, the expression is $0$ for every such $b,c$.
If $a\ne0$, the radicand is nonnegative precisely when $t=b/c\le0$.
On this domain, extract the square: $\sqrt{(a^3t)^2(-t)}=|a^3|\,|t|\sqrt{-t}$.
Since $t\le0$, $|t|=-t$. The result is $-|a^3|\frac bc\sqrt{-b/c}$.
problems.answer: For $a\ne0$, $c\ne0$, $b/c\le0$: $-|a^3|\frac bc\sqrt{-b/c}$ (option ბ). If $a=0$, the original value is $0$.
problems.note: The case $a=0$ matters: the original radical is then defined even if $b/c>0$, whereas the displayed extracted-radical formula would contain an undefined real square root. Handle that zero case separately.

problems.title: Rationalise three denominators
problems.question: Evaluate $\frac2{\sqrt3-1}+\frac3{\sqrt3-2}+\frac{15}{3-\sqrt3}$.
problems.idea: Multiply each fraction by the conjugate of its denominator.
steps: Add the constants: $1-6+15/2=5/2$. Add radical coefficients: $1-3+5/2=1/2$.
